stories.headline: GSTAT allows transitional ITC on truck chassis bought before GST
points: GSTAT Thiruvananthapuram allowed Rs. 1,75,916.79 transitional ITC on a truck chassis bought under Kerala VAT in June 2017.
It held that missing Form 25B before GST did not defeat the claim, as the truck was put to use only after GST began.
A separate Rs. 84,500 claim was rejected because the final VAT return showed a NIL credit balance.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows how transitional credit under Section 140 is judged, and why claims must match the credit balance in earlier returns.
stories.source_title: Goods and Services Tax | Capital Goods ITC Cannot Be Denied for Pre-GST Form 25B Non-Compliance: GSTAT Thiruvananthapuram

stories.headline: Calcutta HC: FERA penalty appeals can go as criminal appeals
points: Calcutta HC rejected the ED's objection that such appeals must be filed on the Original Side as civil revenue matters.
Court held that repeal of FERA did not end accrued penal liabilities or the related procedural remedies.
Four appeals against a ₹2 lakh penalty will be heard on merits on 11 December 2026; merits not decided yet.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how repealed laws, saving clauses and the General Clauses Act affect pending cases, a point relevant to FEMA and law studies.
stories.source_title: Fema / RBI | FERA Penalty Appeals Maintainable as Criminal Appeals Despite FEMA: Calcutta HC
check_notes: The tag 'Corporate Law' doesn't match the source's category (FEMA / RBI). This is a labelling mismatch, not a factual error.

Point 2 stays very close to the source's wording ('repeal did not extinguish accrued penal liabilities or the associated procedural remedies'). It changes enough words that it isn't a copied sentence, but it could be rephrased more.

stories.headline: Gujarat HC quashes reopening order that went beyond show-cause notice
points: Gujarat HC quashed a Section 148A(3) order and the Section 148 notice for AY 2020-21, both dated 30 June 2026.
The notice had questioned transactions of Rs.3,87,87,00,000; the order raised new issues on a loan and Section 40(a)(ia).
The Court found no chance was given to answer the new issues, but allowed a fresh show-cause notice if legally permissible.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows that reopening under Section 148A must stick to the grounds in the show-cause notice and give the assessee a fair hearing.
stories.source_title: Income Tax | Reopening Order Beyond Show-Cause Grounds Quashed for Denial of Opportunity: Gujarat HC
